Complainant Versus M/S Apollo Pharmacy through its Ar Mr.Jayvardhan Binjola Shop No.19, Old Market, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi. .............. Accused Offence pu nishable under Section - 417 read with Section - 416 of The Delhi Municipal Corporation Act,1957 1. By way of the present Judgment, this court shall dispose off challan bearing No. 275/2024, of Apollo Pharmacy located at shop no. 19, Old market, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi dated 05.02.2024 against Mr. Jayvardhan Binjola (Authorized Representative of Apollo pharmacy), under section-417 of Municipal Corporation Act, 1957 (hereinafter referred to as "DMC Act"). BRIEF FACTS: 2.
texts.facts: It is alleged against the accused that the pharmacy shop namely, Apollo Pharmacy located at shop no. 19, Old market, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi dated 05.02.24 was found being running without a valid MCD Health Trade License (HTL) within the jurisdiction of South district in contravention of DMC Act, thereby accused has committed the offence punishable under Section-417 read with Section-461 of DMC Act. It was the defence of the accused that the shop trade in pharmaceutical items and is being run, after taking a valid licence from the Drug Control Department as per the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940.
texts.arguments: The counsel argued that as per Section-417 of DMC Act the accused is not required to get any license from the MCD since the pharmaceutical items falls under item-21 of the Eleven Schedule, which does not mentions sale or trade as one of the necessary criteria for obtaining licence. The counsel for the accused has relied on a judgment pronounced by this court titled as SDMC vs M/S Apollo Hospital Enterprises Ltd. MCD Challan No. 36580 dated 22.08.2015 in support of his arguments.

12. In view of above settled law, this court is of the opinion that there is merit in the argument of the accused and the accused does not require any license for 'trade' of pharmaceutical or medical products from his shop in question.
13. Now coming to the other argument of the accused that the shop of the accused can trade in cosmetics and baby food products, in small quantity as per the proviso to Section-417 of the DMC Act.
It is clear from bare perusal of the Section-417 that the permission of the Commissioner of the MCD is required trade, storage and health purposes.

While the Commissioner may issue 'General Trade License' for all the purposes mention in Part-1 and 'Storage license' for those in Part-2 of the Eleventh Scheldule as per section-417(1)(a) and (d) respectively.
It also has power to issue license to restrain certain activities so to prevent nuisance on account of it being dangerous to life, health and property under section-417(1)(b).
And for all this purpose the Commissioner has been given explicit power under Section-417(3) to fix fees to be paid in respect of premises licensed under sub-section (1).

In the instant case, although the shop in question is primarily trading in pharmaceutical or medicinal products but it is also dealing in grocery items like toothpaste, cerelac, chocolates among others which is also admitted by the accused
There is also PW1/C which goes on to show that a license is required to be obtained from the MCD to run a chemist shop just like the shop in question.

The Commissioner of the MCD, in exercise of its power under Section-417(3) had issued circular Ex.PW1/C in which fees for both "Kiryana goods" at serial no. 50 and "Sale of Pharmaceuticals or Chemist Shop" at serial no. 55 has been prescrib
Although, no 'licence for trade' is required for trade of pharmaceutical products only, strictly speaking as discussed in the foregoing paragraphs.

But harmonious interpretation of Ex.PW1/B with section-417(1)(a), shows that Ex.PW1/B has been issued to deal with such shops where miscellaneous products are being sold in addition to the pharmaceuticals or medical products.
